subject: Request failures observed on rw-lite-8k: mitigation plan & customer guidance
messages:
From: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@horizonretail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Horizon Retail Platform <platform@horizonretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Increased failures from rw-lite-8k today

Irene,

We started seeing ~3% of requests returning 502/504 for rw-lite-8k earlier this morning (US-East). The failures are intermittent but spike during short bursts of traffic (checkout recommender traffic). Attaching a small log excerpt.

Can you confirm whether this is a known degradation and whether there are immediate mitigations we should apply (retries, routing to a different model variant, etc.)? Our SRE is on call and standing by.

Thanks,
Sam Ortega
Sr. Platform Engineer
Horizon Retail

Attachment: rw-lite-8k-error-sample.log (text)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@horizonretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increased failures from rw-lite-8k today

Sam — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We're seeing the same elevated 5xx rate from rw-lite-8k in US-East across our infra monitoring. Early triage notes:
- failures correlate with elevated tail latency on the model workers (85th-99th percentile spikes)
- KV cache misses are higher for these traffic patterns (short prompts + token streaming)
- no hardware alerts (GPUs healthy), appears to be an execution path regression we recently rolled on rw-lite-8k kernel selector

Immediate actions we're recommending while we investigate:
1) Add a 500ms client-side retry with exponential backoff (max 2 retries). This mitigates most transient 5xx during busy bursts.
2) If you have pinned traffic to rw-lite-8k, consider routing critical checkouts to rw-lite-4k (compatible variant) for the next 12 hours.
3) Turn on our streaming=false flag for high-throughput checkout endpoints (reduces KV pressure).

We'll follow up with a timeline for rollback/patch. I'm looping in Marcus and Hannah for the remediation plan.

- Irene
Irene Choi
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@horizonretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increased failures from rw-lite-8k today

Quick ops update from runtime: we see a config change roll at 2026-10-18T02:12:00Z that adjusted kernel selection thresholds for sequences > 2k tokens. That change can amplify tail latency when prefix cache hit rate is low. I'm proposing a hotfix rollback of the selector thresholds for rw-lite-8k, and we can back that out once we have a controlled improved selector.

Planned steps (I'M on it):
- 15:55 PT: enact selector threshold rollback for US-East rw-lite-8k pool (rolling restart, preserving active sessions)
- 16:10 PT: monitor 5xx rate and tail latency for 30 minutes
- 16:45 PT: if error rate < 0.5%, keep rollback; else escalate to full model rollback

I'll attach the mitigation playbook and a short checklist.

Attachment: rw-lite-mitigation-playbook.pdf (2 pages)

-marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@horizonretail.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T16:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increased failures from rw-lite-8k today

Update: Marcus executed the selector rollback at 15:55 PT. Initial telemetry looks promising — 5xx rate dropped from ~3% to ~0.4% within two minutes. We continued to see small blips tied to bursts with large concurrency, so I recommended the client-side retry + streaming=false to Sam (email below).

If the numbers hold for 90 minutes we'll mark this mitigated and start a short root-cause analysis (postmortem). I'll collect traces and kernel decision logs for the affected period.

-Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@horizonretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident note — rw-lite-8k transient 5xxs (summarized)

Sam — wanted to follow up now that we've completed the immediate RCA work and initial postmortem draft. Summary and customer-facing guidance below: 

Timeline (summary):
- 2026-10-18 02:12:00Z — internal kernel selector thresholds changed for rw-lite-8k (deploy)
- 2026-10-18 14:00 PT — Horizon reports 502/504 spike (~3% of requests)
- 2026-10-18 15:55 PT — selector threshold rollback enacted; rapid reduction in 5xx to ~0.3%
- 2026-10-18 16:50 PT — mitigation confirmed; monitoring window continued

Customer impact: brief increase in 5xx and timeouts for traffic routed to rw-lite-8k during bursts; Horizon's checkout flow saw retries added by their SRE which helped recover UX. No data exposure or persistence impact.

Root cause (technical): an aggressive selector configuration introduced at deploy caused higher-than-expected kernel invocation costs for certain short-prefix streaming workloads, increasing tail latency and causing upstream timeouts.

Actions taken:
- Rolled back selector thresholds for rw-lite-8k in US-East (immediate mitigation)
- Updated our deploy gating to include TTLed kernel decision A/B checks for high-throughput workloads
- Published a short customer playbook (attached) with recommended client-side retry patterns and fallback configuration (rw-lite-4k variant)

Follow-ups (tracker items):
- Engineering: create automated selector validation tests for streaming + short prefix patterns (ETA: 2 weeks)
- Product/Docs: add guidance in model compatibility docs about streaming and KV cache patterns (ETA: 1 week)
- Customer success: offer a 1:1 review of Horizon routing to reduce reliance on a single variant during peak traffic (Irene to schedule)

Attachments: rw-lite-mitigation-playbook.pdf, logs excerpt (provided earlier)

If you'd like, we can set up a brief call to walk through the technical findings and the recommended routing changes. Thanks again for the quick signal — it helped us trace the regression faster.

Best,
Irene Choi
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
